category: Russian e-wallet (payment rail used by CIS file hosts and resellers)

free_tier.stated: not applicable: a payment rail, not a retrieval service

interface_detail: Was a wallet app and a merchant payment form; as of 2024-02-21 top-ups and withdrawals stopped after the banking licence was revoked.
tooling: None usable for a new payment.
chaining: Several CIS services still list 'QIWI' among their payment methods (Megaseed.kz lists QIWI KZT and QIWI RUB Turbobit's reseller directory lists Qiwi). Those listings are stale: the rail stopped working in Russia on 2024-02-21.

limits.value: wallet top-up and withdrawal stopped on 2024-02-21 when the Central Bank revoked the licence of QIWI Bank

limits_note: The wallet brand later moved to a new domain (qiwiwall) per RIA, but a moved brand is not a working top-up rail for a foreign buyer.
binding_note: No quota applies: the rail is closed. Any service that lists QIWI today is listing a payment method a buyer cannot fund.

identity_cost.detail: A Russian wallet, funded by Russian rails; after the licence revocation the funding path itself is closed.

reliability_note: Funds in QIWI wallets were not covered by deposit insurance and claims go into the third creditor queue, per the DIA procedure reported in 2024.
confidence_note: The licence revocation and the stopped top-up/withdrawal are quoted from Interfax-Russia's report of 2024-02-21, read today. The later domain move is a RIA headline seen in search, not read in full. Evidence dates normalised to the read date on 2026-10-23; a source that carries its own date keeps it in the proved field.

evidence.proved: 'Клиенты кредитного учреждения не могут пополнить кошельки и вывести с них средства' after the Central Bank revoked the QIWI Bank licence on 2024-02-21
a live CIS service still lists 'QIWI KZT' and 'QIWI RUB' among its payment anchors - the stale-listing case this record exists to flag

notes: A dead rail, recorded because a reader will otherwise treat 'QIWI accepted' on a provider page as a working payment option. The rule this establishes: a payment method listed by a CIS service is a claim about the past, and must be checked against the rail's own status. QIWI KZT may still work in Kazakhstan; nothing was found either way, so the record does not claim it.
